title: Selectors & re-renders
objective: Master the one render-performance rule in zustand: a component re-renders when its selected slice changes by Object.is — and learn when you need useShallow or a custom equality fn.

quiz.prompt: A component reads `useStore((state) => ({ a: state.a, b: state.b }))` from a v5 `create` store. As soon as it mounts, React throws "Maximum update depth exceeded" even though neither a nor b changes. Why, and what is the fix?

options.text: You must call set with replace:true to stop the loop.
The selector builds a new object each call, so Object.is is always false and the update loops until it throws; wrap it in useShallow.
zustand re-renders all subscribers on every set; the loop is inherent and there is no fix.

quiz.prompt: Your slice is `{ user: { name } }` and only `name` changed (a new inner object). You used `useShallow`. Does it prevent the re-render?

options.text: Yes — useShallow deep-compares, so identical names mean no re-render.
No — shallow only compares one level, and the inner user object is a new reference, so it counts as changed.
